Map each node in every diagram on the provided canvas to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change any diagram’s text or the canvas layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (surface):
Map d1 all nodes. Read relevant ranges with line numbers. Return JSON mappings; cover declarations fully as requested.

   829	pub fn deinit(self: *Surface) void {
   830	    // Stop search thread
   831	    if (self.search) |*s| s.deinit();
   832	
   833	    // Stop rendering thread
   834	    {
   835	        self.renderer_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   836	            log.err("error notifying renderer thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   837	        self.renderer_thr.join();
   838	    }
   839	
   840	    // Stop our IO thread
   841	    {
   842	        self.io_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   844	        self.io_thr.join();
   845	    }

   847	    // We need to deinit AFTER everything is stopped, since there are
   848	    // shared values between the two threads.
   849	    //
   850	    // The renderer must be deinitialized before the renderer thread:
   851	    // on macOS the renderer's display link callback points at the
   852	    // thread's `draw_now` handle, and the renderer's deinit is what
   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();
   855	    self.renderer_thread.deinit();
   856	    self.io_thread.deinit();
   857	    self.mouse.selection_gesture.deinit(&self.io.terminal);
   858	    self.io.deinit();

   860	    if (self.inspector) |v| {
   861	        v.deinit(self.alloc);
   862	        self.alloc.destroy(v);
   863	    }
   864	
   865	    // Clean up our keyboard state
   866	    for (self.keyboard.sequence_queued.items) |req| req.deinit();
   867	    self.keyboard.sequence_queued.deinit(self.alloc);

   829	pub fn deinit(self: *Surface) void {
   830	    // Stop search thread
   831	    if (self.search) |*s| s.deinit();
   832	
   833	    // Stop rendering thread
   834	    {
   835	        self.renderer_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   836	            log.err("error notifying renderer thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   837	        self.renderer_thr.join();
   838	    }
   839	
   840	    // Stop our IO thread
   841	    {
   842	        self.io_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   844	        self.io_thr.join();
   845	    }
   846	
   847	    // We need to deinit AFTER everything is stopped, since there are
   848	    // shared values between the two threads.
   849	    //
   850	    // The renderer must be deinitialized before the renderer thread:
   851	    // on macOS the renderer's display link callback points at the
   852	    // thread's `draw_now` handle, and the renderer's deinit is what
   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();
   855	    self.renderer_thread.deinit();
   856	    self.io_thread.deinit();
   857	    self.mouse.selection_gesture.deinit(&self.io.terminal);
   858	    self.io.deinit();
   859	
   860	    if (self.inspector) |v| {
   861	        v.deinit(self.alloc);
   862	        self.alloc.destroy(v);
   863	    }
   864	
   865	    // Clean up our keyboard state
   866	    for (self.keyboard.sequence_queued.items) |req| req.deinit();
   867	    self.keyboard.sequence_queued.deinit(self.alloc);
   868	    self.keyboard.table_stack.deinit(self.alloc);
   869	
   870	    // Clean up our font grid
   871	    self.app.font_grid_set.deref(self.font_grid_key);
   872	
   873	    // Clean up our render state
   874	    if (self.renderer_state.preedit) |p| self.alloc.free(p.codepoints);
   875	    self.alloc.destroy(self.renderer_state.mutex);
   876	    self.config.deinit();
   877	
   878	    log.info("surface closed id={x}", .{self.id});
   879	}

     1	//! Represents the "writer" thread for terminal IO. The reader side is
     2	//! handled by the Termio struct itself and dependent on the underlying
     3	//! implementation (i.e. if its a pty, manual, etc.).
     4	//!
     5	//! The writer thread does handle writing bytes to the pty but also handles
     6	//! different events such as starting synchronized output, changing some
     7	//! modes (like linefeed), etc. The goal is to offload as much from the
     8	//! reader thread as possible since it is the hot path in parsing VT
     9	//! sequences and updating terminal state.
    10	//!
    11	//! This thread state can only be used by one thread at a time.
    12	pub const Thread = @This();
    13	
    14	const std = @import("std");
    15	const ArenaAllocator = std.heap.ArenaAllocator;
    16	const builtin = @import("builtin");
    17	const global = @import("../global.zig");
    18	const xev = global.xev;
    19	const crash = @import("../crash/main.zig");
    20	const internal_os = @import("../os/main.zig");
    21	const termio = @import("../termio.zig");
    22	const renderer = @import("../renderer.zig");
    23	
    24	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    25	const log = std.log.scoped(.io_thread);
    26	
    27	/// This stores the information that is coalesced.
    28	const Coalesce = struct {
    29	    /// The number of milliseconds to coalesce certain messages like resize for.
    30	    /// Not all message types are coalesced.
    31	    const min_ms = 25;
    32	
    33	    resize: ?renderer.Size = null,
    34	};
    35	
    36	/// The number of milliseconds before we reset the synchronized output flag
    37	/// if the running program hasn't already.
    38	const sync_reset_ms = 1000;
    39	
    40	/// The number of milliseconds between each movement during selection scrolling.
    41	const selection_scroll_ms = 15;
    42	
    43	/// Allocator used for some state
    44	alloc: std.mem.Allocator,
    45	
    46	/// The main event loop for the thread. The user data of this loop
    47	/// is always the allocator used to create the loop. This is a convenience
    48	/// so that users of the loop always have an allocator.
    49	loop: xev.Loop,
    50	
    51	/// The completion to use for the wakeup async handle that is present
    52	/// on the termio.Writer.
    53	wakeup_c: xev.Completion = .{},
    54	
    55	/// This can be used to stop the thread on the next loop iteration.
    56	stop: xev.Async,
    57	stop_c: xev.Completion = .{},
    58	
    59	/// This is used for timer-based selection scrolling.
    60	scroll: xev.Timer,
    61	scroll_c: xev.Completion = .{},
    62	scroll_active: bool = false,
    63	
    64	/// This is used to coalesce resize events.
    65	coalesce: xev.Timer,
    66	coalesce_c: xev.Completion = .{},
    67	coalesce_cancel_c: xev.Completion = .{},
    68	coalesce_data: Coalesce = .{},

    70	/// This timer is used to reset synchronized output modes so that
    71	/// the terminal doesn't freeze with a bad actor.
    72	sync_reset: xev.Timer,
    73	sync_reset_c: xev.Completion = .{},
    74	sync_reset_cancel_c: xev.Completion = .{},
    75	
    76	flags: packed struct {
    77	    /// This is set to true only when an abnormal exit is detected. It
    78	    /// tells our mailbox system to drain and ignore all messages.
    79	    drain: bool = false,
    80	
    81	    /// True if linefeed mode is enabled. This is duplicated here so that the
    82	    /// write thread doesn't need to grab a lock to check this on every write.
    83	    linefeed_mode: bool = false,
    84	
    85	    /// This is true when the inspector is active.
    86	    has_inspector: bool = false,
    87	} = .{},

    89	/// Initialize the thread. This does not START the thread. This only sets
    90	/// up all the internal state necessary prior to starting the thread. It
    91	/// is up to the caller to start the thread with the threadMain entrypoint.

    94	) !Thread {

    96	    var loop = try xev.Loop.init(.{});
    97	    errdefer loop.deinit();
    98	
    99	    // This async handle is used to stop the loop and force the thread to end.
   100	    var stop_h = try xev.Async.init();
   101	    errdefer stop_h.deinit();
   102	
   103	    // This timer is used for selection scrolling.
   104	    var scroll_h = try xev.Timer.init();
   105	    errdefer scroll_h.deinit();
   106	
   107	    // This timer is used to coalesce resize events.
   108	    var coalesce_h = try xev.Timer.init();
   109	    errdefer coalesce_h.deinit();
   110	
   111	    // This timer is used to reset synchronized output modes.
   112	    var sync_reset_h = try xev.Timer.init();
   113	    errdefer sync_reset_h.deinit();

   116	        .alloc = alloc,
   117	        .loop = loop,
   118	        .stop = stop_h,
   119	        .scroll = scroll_h,
   120	        .coalesce = coalesce_h,
   121	        .sync_reset = sync_reset_h,
   122	    };

   126	/// completes executing; the caller must join prior to this.

   131	    self.stop.deinit();

     6	//! different events such as starting synchronized output, changing some
     7	//! modes (like linefeed), etc. The goal is to offload as much from the
     8	//! reader thread as possible since it is the hot path in parsing VT
     9	//! sequences and updating terminal state.

    30	    /// Not all message types are coalesced.
    31	    const min_ms = 25;
    32	
    33	    resize: ?renderer.Size = null,
    34	};
    35	
    36	/// The number of milliseconds before we reset the synchronized output flag
    37	/// if the running program hasn't already.

    39	
    40	/// The number of milliseconds between each movement during selection scrolling.
    41	const selection_scroll_ms = 15;

    43	/// Allocator used for some state
    44	alloc: std.mem.Allocator,

    47	/// is always the allocator used to create the loop. This is a convenience
    48	/// so that users of the loop always have an allocator.
    49	loop: xev.Loop,

   177	                    \\Please free up some pty devices and try again.

   183

   189	                    \\was too large, or the underlying pty failed to accept
   190	                    \\the write.
   191	                    \\
   192	                    \\Ghostty can't continue since it can't guarantee that
   193	                    \\initial terminal state will be as desired. Please review
   194	                    \\the value of `input` in your configuration file and
   195	                    \\ensure that all the path values exist and are readable.
   196	                ;
   197	
   198	                t.eraseDisplay(.complete, false);
   199	                t.printString(str) catch {};
   200	            },

   208	                    \\If this looks like a bug, please report it.

   211	                ,
   212	                    .{err},

   216	
   217	                t.eraseDisplay(.complete, false);
   218	                t.printString(str) catch {};
